newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Huge diesel purchase, jet plunges.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Huge diesel purchase, jet plunges.

text.p: A looming slide in Singapore gas oil price was curbed on Tuesday when two local traders bought a whopping 1.35 million barrels, bringing their total purchases so far to nearly 10 million barrels, leaving traders scratching their heads.

Market sources estimate that the local traders would have to pay a staggering US$300 million for the cargoes that they have bought since March 3. The market remained uncertain when the local firms would end their buying spree.
But sellers with arbitrage cargoes were only too pleased to unload their cargoes at firm levels, even though values have slipped about $1.00 since last week.

Traders said the nine cargoes traded for end April to early May liftings at between $26.20 and $27.00, did not show a clear market direction at a time when regional demand was said to be soft and should have slipped below $26.00 if not for the persistent buying by the local traders.
Swaps reflected the real market sentiment, falling another 10 cents per barrel with April last quoted at $26.05/$26.30, and May at $24.90/$25.05.

Vietnam bought 170,000 tonnes of diesel in its tender for teh second quarter at 10 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quote free-on-board (fob) and 95 cents to $1.15 per barrel premiums cost-and-freight Vietnam.

Jet fuel prices plunged with two cargoes traded. A US trader bought 200,000 barrels at $24.00 per barrel for April 25-30 lifting c-and-f basis, and sold 100,000 barrels to a Singapore trader at $24.75 for April 29-May 3 lifting fob.
Jet fuel values have plunged almost $3.00 since March 18, reflecting the soft regional demand.
